company.value: Retool is an enterprise application-development platform for building governed internal apps and automations. Retool says its platform can generate production-ready applications, connect to production data, and deploy with authentication, access controls, audit logging, and governance. It also describes core use cases spanning CRUD apps, workflows/automations, and enterprise-operations software.

funding.value: The latest publicly announced financing located was a $45,000,000 Series C2 at a $3,200,000,000 valuation, announced by Retool on 2022-07-28T13:00:00Z. Retool named existing investors including Sequoia Capital, John Collison, Patrick Collison, Nat Friedman, Elad Gil, Daniel Gross, and Caryn Marooney.

hiring_signals.value: Retool’s careers page showed 32 open roles at fetch time, including engineering, product, and sales-development openings. This is direct evidence of active hiring, although it does not establish planned hire volume.

A Staff Product Manager, Automation opening says Retool is defining and scaling next-generation automation across workflows, integrations, and AI-driven agents, with the goal of extending beyond internal apps into end-to-end process orchestration.

An Enterprise Platform product role and a Governance engineering role indicate investment in deployment infrastructure, permissions, auditability, AI-agent controls, data-access policies, and enterprise security/governance.

An enterprise AE posting describes enterprise as Retool’s largest-by-revenue segment and references six- and seven-figure deals. A BDR posting says the sales team grew 3× in the prior year and that Retool is expanding outbound capacity toward 2026 revenue targets.

likely_use_case.value: Retool is likely evaluating or could build a custom, governed SDR qualification/research workflow that connects approved sales data sources with AI-assisted research and internal automations. This is an inference from Retool’s app/automation platform, MCP capability, and stated governance features—not evidence of a packaged SDR-research product or current internal adoption by its SDR team.

deal_band.value: Enterprise / strategic: Retool’s own enterprise-AE role references six- and seven-figure deals and identifies enterprise as its largest-by-revenue segment. This indicates that large enterprise deal sizes are part of its sales motion, but does not establish the size of any prospective research-automation purchase.

unverified: A first-party, point-in-time total employee count was not found.

A primary Retool source explicitly designating its corporate headquarters was not found; Built In lists San Francisco, while Retool confirms offices in San Francisco, New York, Salt Lake City, and London.
An authoritative formal company-stage designation was not found.
No primary announcement of financing after the 2022-07-28T13:00:00Z Series C2 was located; this does not rule out later undisclosed financings, debt, or secondary transactions.
The current availability of Retool’s MCP server for self-hosted deployments requires confirmation because Retool’s first-party materials conflict.
No evidence was found that Retool currently uses a specific SDR research-automation tool or that it is actively purchasing one.

positions: LeadIQ lists approximately 416 employees as of 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z and a 201–500 employee band.
conflicts.resolution: Neither is a first-party workforce disclosure. LeadIQ provides a stated observation period, but both should be treated as third-party estimates rather than definitive current headcount.

positions: Retool’s directly fetched careers page displayed 32 open roles.
A separately fetched search-result representation for the same careers URL stated 38 roles.
conflicts.resolution: The direct careers-page result is more reliable than a search-index snippet. The difference may reflect stale indexing or a page change and cannot be resolved from the fetched evidence.

conflicts.field: total funding and number of rounds
positions: Startup Intros reports $141,000,000 across five rounds.
Tracxn reports $165,000,000 across six rounds, including a separate $30,000,000 2021 Series B entry.
conflicts.resolution: Neither database total is a complete primary-source funding record. Retool’s disclosed $50,000,000 Series B and the arithmetic of the five reported rounds favor the $141,000,000 sequence for those reported rounds, but this does not establish complete lifetime funding.

positions: Retool and TechCrunch call the $45,000,000 financing a Series C2.
Tracxn classifies the same financing as Series C.
conflicts.resolution: Use Series C2 because Retool’s own announcement is the stronger source for its financing nomenclature; note that some databases normalize it to Series C.

conflicts.field: MCP server availability for self-hosted customers
positions: Retool’s 2026-05-08T00:00:00Z launch post says the MCP server was available to Cloud and self-hosted customers.
A later Retool guide says the native MCP server is in public beta on Cloud/all plans and that self-hosted access is coming in a future stable release.
conflicts.resolution: The later guide is more specific about present deployment availability, but the first-party sources conflict. Verify current self-hosted availability in live documentation before relying on it.

brief.suggested_opening: How is the SDR organization planning to operationalize research before qualification calls—especially where research needs to pull from approved internal data sources and remain governed?
